language.heading: Language
language.description: Language is per-device — it won't sync to your other devices. Pollis starts in your system language when we ship it, and English otherwise.

appearance.heading: Appearance
appearance.description: Terminal is the default IRC/monospace look. Refined is a friendlier, proportional-sans layout for people who prefer a more conventional chat app. Syncs across your devices.

display.heading: Display (this device)
display.fontSizeNote: Font size is per-device — it won't sync to your other devices.
display.fontSizeSample: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
display.callRingtoneDescription: Plays a looping ring on this device when someone calls. Off here doesn't mute the alert badge or your other devices.

layout.heading: Layout
layout.sidebarDescription: Controls whether the left sidebar is open when the app starts. Toggle ad-hoc with {{shortcut}}.
layout.rightPanelDescription: Members and shared media for the channel or conversation you're viewing. Remembered on this device for your account — it stays as you leave it while you move around the app, and doesn't follow you to your other devices. Toggle it any time with {{shortcut}}.
layout.closeToTrayDescription: When on, closing the window hides Pollis to the system tray instead of quitting. Right-click the tray icon to quit. If your desktop environment doesn't show tray icons (bare GNOME without the AppIndicator extension), turn this off.
layout.menubarIconDescription: Adds a Pollis icon to the macOS menu bar (top right). Click it to open the window, mute the mic while in a call, or quit the app. Off by default — the dock icon already keeps Pollis reachable when the window is closed.

readReceipts.heading: Read receipts
readReceipts.description: In direct messages, lets the people you are talking to see when their messages reached your device and when you read them. Turning this off also hides their receipts from you — you will no longer see whether your own messages were delivered or read. Receipts are end-to-end encrypted like any message; our servers never see who read what. Group channels never send receipts.

retention.heading: Local message history
retention.description: Controls how much message history is kept on this device. Older messages are deleted from local storage to save space. This does not affect your other devices or the people you're talking to, and you'll still receive new messages normally.

overlay.heading: Network privacy (relay)
overlay.description: Routes Pollis's own traffic (messages, sync) through a relay so our servers see the relay's address, not yours. Calls connect directly. This hides your IP from Pollis — it is not anonymity, and does not change end-to-end encryption.
overlay.itemPrefer: <mode>Prefer</mode> — Use the relay when available; fall back to a direct connection if it isn't.
overlay.itemStrict: <mode>Strict</mode> — Only connect through the relay. If no relay is reachable, sending is paused rather than revealing your IP.

relayServing.heading: Run a relay for others
relayServing.intro: A separate choice from the setting above. That one decides whether <dim>your</dim> traffic goes through a relay. This one decides whether <dim>other people's</dim> traffic goes through <dim>your device</dim>. Turning on either never turns on the other.
relayServing.enabledLabel: Relay traffic for other Pollis users
relayServing.enabledDescription: Off unless you switch it on. You can switch it back off at any time.
relayServing.wouldDoBody: It forwards other people's already-encrypted traffic on to Pollis's own servers, so those servers see your address for that traffic instead of theirs. Your device only ever forwards to Pollis's servers — never to anyone else's, and never to the open internet.
relayServing.wouldSeeBody: Nothing. Relaying grants no read access of any kind. What passes through is a sealed stream your device holds no key to: you can't read messages, files or calls, you can't see who sent them or who they're for, and you can't tell one kind of traffic from another. All your device learns is that some Pollis client is exchanging encrypted bytes with a Pollis server. You also can't alter anything in transit — tampering only breaks the connection, which the sender routes around.
relayServing.costBody: Bandwidth, and — without the conditions below — battery and metered data.
relayServing.exactBody: To be exact about what relaying buys: it hides IP addresses from our servers. That is the whole of it. It is not anonymity, it is no defence against someone who can watch both ends of a connection, and it does not hide who talks to whom — our servers still see that from the account making the request, relay or no relay. It is also not what makes Pollis end-to-end encrypted: your messages are encrypted on the sending device whether or not anyone runs a relay. Relaying is metadata protection layered underneath that guarantee, never the evidence for it.
relayServing.wifiOnlyDescription: Stops relaying on cellular, or on any connection your device reports as metered. On by default.
relayServing.powerOnlyDescription: Stops relaying while this device is running on battery. On by default.
relayServing.statusUnreportable: this build can't report relay status, so Pollis can't confirm whether this device is relaying.
relayServing.statusUnsupported: relaying isn't available on this device.
relayServing.statusServing_one: relaying — carrying {{count}} connection, {{bytes}} forwarded since Pollis started.
relayServing.statusServing_other: relaying — carrying {{count}} connections, {{bytes}} forwarded since Pollis started.
relayServing.holdNoInboundPath: paused — other devices can't reach this one through your network
relayServing.applyError: Couldn't apply this to the running app: {{error}}. Your choice is saved and takes effect once the relay service is reachable.

user.title: User Settings
user.verificationCodeRequired: Enter the code from your email.

security.title: Security
security.eventDeviceEnrolledDetail: Device {{device}} was added to your account.
security.eventDeviceEnrolledDetailUnknown: A new device was added to your account.
security.eventDeviceRejectedDetail: A request from device {{device}} was rejected.
security.eventDeviceRejectedDetailUnknown: A device enrollment request was rejected.
security.eventDeviceRevokedDetail: Device {{device}} was signed out and removed from your account.
security.eventDeviceRevokedDetailNamed: {{name}} ({{device}}) was signed out and removed from your account.
security.eventDeviceRevokedDetailUnknown: A device was signed out and removed from your account.
security.eventIdentityResetDetail: You reset your account. All previous devices and groups were orphaned.
security.eventSecretKeyRotatedDetail: Your Secret Key was changed. The old one no longer works.
security.accountKeyDescription: Your identity key is published to a public, append-only log so anyone can confirm contacts are talking to the real you. This checks that the log agrees with the key on this device.
security.buildVerifyGuideLink: How to verify this build independently →
security.thisBuildDescription: Every release Pollis ships is fingerprinted into the same public, append-only log. This confirms the build you're running is one Pollis published there and independently verified by third-party rebuilders — it does not by itself prove the build matches the source, since a tampered app could lie about its own fingerprint.
security.buildVerifyError: Couldn't check this build right now. Try again in a moment.
security.pinDescription: The local PIN unlocks Pollis on this device. It never leaves the device and can't be recovered — use your Secret Key if you forget it.
security.autoLockDescription: Lock Pollis back to the PIN screen after a period with no mouse or keyboard activity, so walking away from this machine doesn't leave your decrypted conversations on screen. You can always lock immediately with {{shortcut}}.
security.autoLockNote: Applies to this device only. A call in progress keeps Pollis unlocked — locking would close the local database out from under the call. Nothing is lost when it locks: your messages are on disk, and entering your PIN brings you straight back.
security.devicesDescription: Every device signed in to your account. Revoke any you don't recognise — the device loses access to all groups and DMs on its next sync.
security.eventsDescription: Every time a device is added to your account, a device is revoked, an enrollment is rejected, or your identity is reset, it shows up here. Check it if you ever suspect someone has accessed your account.
security.revokeMediaOnExitLabel: Revoke system permissions when Pollis quits
security.revokeMediaOnExitDescription: When on, Pollis clears its saved camera / microphone / screen permissions as it quits, so the OS asks again next time.
security.mediaNoteMac: Clears Pollis's saved permission; macOS will ask again next time you use each feature.
security.mediaNoteLinux: Linux grants media access per session — Pollis stores no standing grant, so there's nothing to revoke here.
security.mediaNoteWindows: Camera and microphone status comes from Windows privacy settings. “Revoke now” opens those settings so you can turn Pollis off; screen sharing isn't tracked there.
security.mediaNoteOther: Media permission controls aren't available on this platform.
security.dangerZoneDescription: Permanently delete your account and all associated data. This cannot be undone.

keyChange.heading: Safety number changed
keyChange.body: — {{name}}'s identity key is different from what was pinned. Verify out-of-band before trusting this conversation.

changePin.title: Change PIN
changePin.hintOld: Enter your current 4-digit PIN to continue.
changePin.hintConfirm: Enter the new PIN again to confirm.
changePin.mismatch: New PINs don't match — try again

update.title: Software Update
update.heading: Software Update
update.managedNote: This install is managed by {{manager}}. Pollis can't update itself from inside the app — use your package manager, then relaunch.
